title: Maximum Product of Three Numbers
statement: Choose three entries of the integer array `nums` at three different positions and multiply them together. Return the largest product that any such choice can give.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every triple costs O(n³). After sorting, only two triples can be the best. Three large positives give a large product, so the three biggest values are one candidate. Two negatives multiply to a positive, so the two most negative values (the two smallest) times the biggest value is the other. Every other triple is beaten by one of these two, including when all values are negative or zeros are present.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order and let `n` be its length.
2. `topThree` is the product of the last three values.
3. `twoSmallest` is the product of the first two values and the last value.
4. Return the larger of the two.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, -3]` sorts to `[-3, 1, 2]`. `topThree = 2 · 1 · (-3) = -6` and `twoSmallest = (-3) · 1 · 2 = -6`; with only three numbers both candidates are the same triple, so the answer is `-6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the rest is constant work.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Taking only the three largest values misses `[-10, -10, 5, 2]`, where `-10 · -10 · 5 = 500` wins.
- Using the two smallest with the third smallest is never better: the biggest value is the right partner for them.
- JavaScript's default `sort()` compares as strings; pass `(a, b) => a - b`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `topThree` | product of the three largest values |
| `twoSmallest` | product of the two smallest values and the largest one |

narration.1: The function receives the array; only its extreme values will matter.
narration.2: Sort ascending so the largest and smallest values sit at the two ends.
narration.3: Remember the length to index from the end.
narration.5: First candidate: multiply the three largest values.
narration.6: Second candidate: two most negative values make a positive, so pair them with the largest value.
narration.8: No other triple can beat both candidates, so return the larger one.
